insight.title: How Curiosity Rebuilds the World
insight.subtitle: The quiet art of turning today’s questions into tomorrow’s tools.

sections.text: We are born with a restless desire to improve the tools we hold. It begins as a quiet itch, a tiny whisper asking if a stone could be sharper or a light brighter. This is the seed of change. We don't just inhabit the world; we are constantly reimagining its very foundation.

Innovation happens when an old problem meets a fresh pair of eyes. It is the art of rearranging the familiar into something entirely new. Like a weaver pulling threads, we combine ancient wisdom with modern craft. We take the rhythm of the tides and turn it into warmth for our homes.

This endless cycle of making makes our lives softer and our horizons wider. Every new breakthrough is a gift from the present to the future. It is how we speak to generations we will never meet. We build bridges and craft stories, ensuring that the path ahead is always a little clearer.

news.title: Study finds lysosomes guide the way for ‘leader cells’ during wound healing
news.description: Researchers have discovered that lysosomes, traditionally viewed as cellular waste bins, sense mechanical forces and reposition themselves to the cell's edge to trigger the formation of leader cells essential for tissue repair and embryonic development. | Tata Institute of Fundamental Research Hyder

news.title: Hegseth's remarks highlight the government's reluctance to show human costs of war
news.description: Remarks by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth that the American press emphasizes U.S. casualties in the Iran war because it “wants to make the president look bad” are a reminder of something that has endured across many decades and conflicts: the tension and trepidation about news that reminds Americans of the human cost of war.

news.title: Armed robots take to the battlefield in Ukraine war
news.description: Ukraine has embarked on a programme to deploy armed robots on the battlefield against Russian forces.

news.title: Frequent ejaculation is associated with lower risk of prostate cancer
news.description: Researchers found men who ejaculated more often had fewer prostate cancer diagnoses, pointing to a possible biological explanation.

news.title: Scott Bessent warns the largest bombing campaign on Iran happens ‘tonight’
news.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says Iran is fighting economic warfare after military failures, as U.S. launches bombing campaign against missiles.
